sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: MaximumRetryAttempts default -1, '-1 means infinite: failed records are retried until the record expires'; MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds default -1; BisectBatchOnFunctionError default false; StartingPosition AT_TIMESTAMP, TRIM_HORIZON or LATEST; FunctionResponseTypes ReportBatchItemFailures. sources.cite: AWS Lambda Developer Guide, Retaining discarded batch records for a Kinesis Data Streams event source in Lambda
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-17 (German machine translation of the English page). Relevant text: when the function returns an error Lambda retries until the records expire, exceed MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds or reach MaximumRetryAttempts; BisectBatchOnFunctionError splits a failed batch in two to isolate bad records and splitting does not use up retries; 'with the default settings a bad record can block processing on the affected shard for up to one week'; an on-failure destination can be an SNS topic, SQS queue, S3 bucket or Kafka; for SQS and SNS Lambda sends only metadata (shardId, start and end sequence numbers), so the records must be read from the stream before they expire; for S3 it also sends the whole invocation record as payload.

brief.situation: You are the data engineer on call for Tallis Freight, a fictional trucking company. Truck telematics flow into the Kinesis stream telematics (4 shards, 24-hour retention); the Lambda function enrich-telematics reads it and writes to the S3 data lake. The 07:10 dispatch report is built from last night's data. At 06:10 an alarm fired: the function's IteratorAge is over three hours and still rising.
handover: Night shift says three of the four shards look current; nobody changed the function this week.
Trucks on firmware 4.2 started rolling out at 03:00.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the stream's shards, the function, its failure destination and the data lake.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why one shard stopped, what you changed in the event source mapping, and how the bad record can be replayed.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Ties the stuck shard to one record and the mapping's unlimited retries.
parts.modelAnswer: The function failed on the same truncated record from firmware 4.2 on every attempt; with MaximumRetryAttempts -1 and no destination, Lambda retries that batch until the record expires, so shard-0002 stopped for three hours while the others stayed current.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Bisects, bounds retries and keeps the failure somewhere it can be replayed, without skipping data.
parts.modelAnswer: Turned on bisect on function error, set two retries and an S3 on-failure destination, so the bad record is isolated and kept with its payload and the shard moves on. Starting from LATEST would have dropped three hours of a quarter of the fleet.

parts.label: Replay
parts.criteria: Says how the kept record gets back into the lake and checks the backlog drained.
parts.modelAnswer: IteratorAge fell back to about a second before 07:10; the S3 failure record holds the payload and sequence number, so it can be repaired and replayed once the parser handles firmware 4.2.

expertPath.text: IteratorAge rising since 03:02; the log shows the same batch failing on one truncated record; the mapping has unlimited retries and no destination.
Turn on bisect, two retries and an S3 on-failure destination.
IteratorAge falls; the S3 failure record holds the payload for replay; the backlog clears before 07:10.

skippedData.headline: Fast, and a quarter of the night is gone
skippedData.body: LATEST starts at the tip of each shard. The backlog behind the bad record was never read, and the stream's 24-hour retention will soon remove it. Bisect, bound the retries and keep the failure in a destination instead.

reportMissed.headline: The report ran without a quarter of the fleet
reportMissed.body: Memory, timeouts and more shards do not move a batch that fails on its data. The function's log names the record; the mapping's retry and destination settings decide whether it can block a shard.

fixed.headline: Good: unblock without losing data
fixed.body: You read the error and the mapping before changing anything, isolated the bad record instead of skipping the backlog, kept it with its payload for replay, and confirmed IteratorAge fell before the report.

gaps.headline: Unblocked, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the diagnosis, a destination that keeps the record, the checks, or memory and shard changes that cost money and fixed nothing.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: A shard whose iterator age grows minute for minute while the others stay current is blocked, not slow. The log shows every attempt failing on the same truncated record, and the mapping retries without limit (-1) with no destination, so Lambda will hold that shard until the record expires. Turn on bisect on function error so the bad record is isolated, bound the retries, and send failures to S3, which keeps the payload so the record can be replayed after the parser is fixed. Do not recreate the mapping at LATEST, which skips the backlog, and do not add memory or shards, which change nothing about a record that cannot be parsed. Confirm IteratorAge falls before the 07:10 report.
